**Synopsis:**
Reuters columnist Mike Dolan argues that Trump's incoherent linking of Fed rate policy to trade deficits — threatening to halt trade with countries the US runs deficits with unless rates are cut — has backfired rhetorically and may hand Fed Chair Kevin Warsh a political opening. With a September rate hike already >50% priced into futures, strong payrolls, core inflation above 2% for 65 consecutive months, and Warsh having struck a hawkish tone at Jackson Hole, Dolan contends a 25bps hike would simultaneously reinforce the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, demonstrate Warsh's independence from the White House, and potentially compress long-end yields by reasserting the Fed's anti-inflation commitment.
